ADDRESS OF.description: The ADDRESS OF special register references the address of a data item in the linkage section, the local-storage section, or the working-storage section.

ADD.description: ADD a TO b GIVING c

ADD CORRESPONDING.description: ADD CORRESPONDING is used to add the corresponding variables or fields in two identical group variables

ADD OVERFLOW.description: ADD literal TO var ON OVERFLOW error-logic

ADVANCING.description: The WRITE AFTER ADVANCING phrase in the PROCEDURE DIVISION gives the COBOL programmer control over report file processing/pagination. Note that OUTPUT-RECORD-FILE-STATUS-CODE is a variable you code in your program that automates the process of validating each I/O action. z/OS update its value after each action. The field must be defined in the file FD and declared as a two-byte PIC XX field in the PROCEDURE DIVISION. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

ANYCASE.description: ANYCASE is used in conjunction with intrinsic functions to make string manipulation case-insensitive.

AREA.description: The AREA/AREAS keywords pertain to the reuse of main storage. (ie. They force z/OS to use the same main storage area for performing internal file processing.) The three instances are syntax checked, but have no effect on the program at run-time.

BEFORE ADVANCING.description: The WRITE BEFORE phrase in the PROCEDURE DIVISION gives the COBOL programmer control over file (most often report file) processing pagination. Note that OUTPUT-RECORD-FILE-STATUS-CODE must be defined in the file FD and declared as a two-byte (PIC XX) field in the WORKING-STORAGE. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

BIT TO CHAR.description: Function used to populate an PIC X/PIC A field with binary data.

BLANK WHEN ZERO.description: BLANK WHEN ZERO specifies that an elementary field will contains spaces when its value is zero.

BLOCK.description: BLOCK CONTAINS clause (in the DATA DIVISION, file FD) dictates the size of the physical (I/O) records. By coding BLOCK CONTAINS 0  z/os will choose the optimal "blocking factor" for most efficient file I/O - taking into account channels, and DASD along with the file specifics.

BOOLEAN.prefix: JSON GENERATE FROM then CONVERT TO BOOLEAN
BOOLEAN.description: BOOLEAN as a reserved word is typically used to convert COBOL data to non-JSON data format.

BOTTOM.description: Part of the DATA DIVISION file FD, LINAGE clause, LINES AT BOTTOM tells COBOL to setup a bottom margin (blank lines at the bottom of every logical page). https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=entries-linage-clause

CALL.description: The CALL statement transfers control from one compiled program to another. Note that the BY and RETURNING clauses are optional. For more on CALL: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=statements-call-statement

CANCEL.description: The CANCEL statement terminates the subprogram. This ensures that data in the subprogram reverts to its initial state the next time the subprogram is called. Also when a CANCEL statement is executed all called programs contained within the program referenced in the CANCEL statement are canceled. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SS6SG3_6.4.0/pdf/pgmvs.pdf

CODE SET.description: CODE-SET is used in the COBOL DATA DIVISION, FILE SECTION, FD CLAUSE. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SS6SG3_6.4.0/pdf/pgmvs.pdf

COLLATING.description: Part of the IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. Note that the default option is EBCDIC

COMP.description: BINARY data and synonyms COMP and COMP-4 are the two's complement data representation in COBOL. Two's complement Hex data (EBCDIC) representation of numeric values in fields within the DATA DIVISION.

COMP-1.description: A four-byte single-precision floating-point number declared in the DATA DIVISION. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=arithmetic-formats-numeric-data

COMP-2.description: A four-byte double-precision floating-point number declared in the DATA DIVISION. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=arithmetic-formats-numeric-data

COMP-3.description: Internally-packed (efficient) number declared in the DATA DIVISION. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=6-packed-decimal-comp-3

COMP-4.description: BINARY data and synonyms COMP and COMP-4 are the two's complement data representation in COBOL. Two's complement Hex data (EBCDIC) representation of numeric values in fields within the DATA DIVISION.

COMP-5.description: Typically used to communicate between Java/C/C++/Python/etc. and COBOL, with COMP-5, data, the size of the variable is defined by the field's PIC size. When numeric data is moved into a COMP-5 item, truncation occurs at the binary field size rather than at the COBOL picture clause declaration. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=arithmetic-formats-numeric-data

body: NOT ON SIZE ERROR GO TO ${7:PROGRAM-FINAL-ACTION}
COMPUTE.description: COMPUTE provides an alebraic-style keyword for the speficiation of complex arithemetic expressions: + (add), - (subtract), * (multiply), / (divide), ** (power of) and any intrinsic functions that return numeric results. ON SIZE ERROR allows you to trap situcations such as divide by zero and result overflow. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=statements-compute-statement

CONFIGURATION.description: The CONFIGURATION SECTION describes the z/OS environment on which the program is compiled and executed. It is an optional section for programs, functions, prototypes, and classes. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=division-configuration-section

CONTAINS.description: A fixed-block file. Note that BLOCK CONTAINS 0 leaves the blocking-optimization up to z/OS - and is the preferred way to specify most QSAM file FDs. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=entries-block-contains-clause

CONTENT-OF.description: The CONTENT-OF intrinsic function produces a temporary copy of the input argument. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=functions-content

CONTROL.description: *CONTROL is a Compiler option - that allows the user to limit (or not limit) the MAP output of a program compile.  https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

CONVERTING.description: CONVERTING is a parameter of the INSPECT keyword - used to replace character values. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=inspect-examples-statement

COPY.description: COPY is used to insert source code - stored in a PDS or SCM into COBOL lines. Note that the JCL or Source Management System (Endevor, etc.) must be available and specified correctly. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

COUNT.description: Part of the UNSTRING verb, COUNT places the number of characters in a numeric variable (VAR-3 in the above example). https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

CRT.description: Part of the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph/CONFIGURATION SECTION in the ENVIRONMENT DIVISION. CRT STATUS returns data regarding the status of a screen-based COBOL ACCEPT statement when an ON EXCEPTION statement is included in the ACCEPT statement.

body: CURRENCY SIGN IS "${1:\$USD}" WITH PICTURE SYMBOL "${2:\$}".
CURRENCY.description: CURRENCY SIGN clause is defined in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph in the CONFIGURATION SECTION/ENVIRONMENT DIVISION. In the given example, the PIC character $ indicates that the currency sign $USD is to be substitued. Note that you may declare multiple curency signs for multiple currencies. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

CURSOR.description: CURSOR IS is the name of a numeric data item described in the WORKING-STORAGE SECTION - that contains a value for placement of the cursor on a CRT. CURSOR IS is defined in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph.

AT DATE.description: AT DATE is used with the IBM COBOL Debugger. It gives the Debugger control for each date processing statement within the specified block. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/developer-for-zos/14.2?topic=command-date-cobol In the above example: Each time a date processing statement is encountered in the compile unit; 1. Display the location of the statement 2. List a specific variable, and 3. Resume running the program.

DATE COMPILED YYYY/MM/DD.description: DATE-COMPILED is an optional statement that describes the specific date of program compilation. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

DATE COMPILED MM/DD/YYYY.description: DATE-COMPILED is an optional statement that describes the specific date of program compilation. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

DATE WRITTEN YYYY/MM/DD.description: DATE-WRITTEN is an optional statement that describes the specific date of program compilation. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

DATE WRITTEN MM/DD/YYYY.description: DATE-WRITTEN is an optional statement that describes the specific date of program compilation. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

DAY.description: The above is an example of utilizing a Julian Date receiving field (PiC 9(5) variable - YY NNN) - from z/OS. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=as-date-date-yyyymmdd-day-day-yyyyddd-day-week-time

DAY OF WEEK.description: The above is an example of utilizing a one-byte(PiC 9(1)receiving variable - (1-7) from z/OS. Note that 1 = Monday, 2 = Tuesday, 3 = Wednesday, etc. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=as-date-date-yyyymmdd-day-day-yyyyddd-day-week-time

DBCS.description: A class-condition, allowing you to test whether the data in a field is in valid DBCS format. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

DECIMAL-POINT.description: Part of the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, the `DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA` clause exchanges the functions of the period and the comma in PIC character-strings and in numeric literals. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

DECLARATIVES 1.description: Declaratives provide one or more special-purpose sections that are executed when an exception occurs. https://www.ibm.com/docs/sl/cobol-zos/6.2?topic=procedures-example-use-debugging

DECLARATIVES 2.description: Declaratives provide one or more special-purpose sections that are executed when an exception occurs. https://www.ibm.com/docs/sl/cobol-zos/6.2?topic=procedures-example-use-debugging

DEFAULT.description: A COBOL Runtime directive to initialize the buffers for QSAM ("flat" files). Note that your Systems Programmer will most likely utilize this keyword.

DEPENDING.description: OCCURS DEPENDING ON (ODO) specifies variable-length internal COBOL tables.  https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SS6SG3_6.4.0/pdf/pgmvs.pdf

DISPLAY-1.description: The DISPLAY-1 phrase defines an item as DBCS. The data item is stored in character form, with each character occupying 2 bytes of storage. https://www.informatik.uni-leipzig.de/cs/Literature/Textbooks/Cobol/LangRefzOS.pdf

body: DIVIDE INTO GIVING REMAINDER=DIVIDE ${1:id} INTO ${2:id} GIVING ${3:id} REMAINDER ${4:id4}

DUPLICATES #1.description: DUPLICATES allows an indexed VSAM file to be defined with duplicate values declared in a defined variable within the record in the FD. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=files-using-alternate-keys

DUPLICATES #2.description: `IN ORDER` forces the z/OS SORT utility to retain the original order of the input file, if duplicate key-field values are found. Note that `IN ORDER` is an optional clause of `WITH DUPLICATES`. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=merge-preserving-original-sequence-records-equal-keys

DYNAMIC.description: Allows the specific READ/WRITE statement to determine the access mode. Records can be processed sequentially or randomly or both. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=files-vsam-dynamic-access-optional-logic-path

IF-ELSE.description: `IF ... ELSE` codes a choice between two COBOL processing actions. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=actions-coding-choice

END.description: Scope terminator - common with many verbs https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=appendixes-reserved-words

ENTER.description: The statement is treated as a comment. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

ENTRY.description: The ENTRY statement establishes an alternate entry point into a COBOL called subprogram. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

body: ENTRY ${1:literal} USING${2| , BY REFERENCE , BY VALUE |}${3:LINKAGE-DATA-ITEM}.

ERROR #1.description: NUMVAR-1 is divided into NUMVAR-2. If `NUMVAR-1 = 0` or if the quotient is larger than NUMVAR-3 the `ON SIZE ERROR` statement is executed. If `ON SIZE ERROR` isn't coded the program ABENDS. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

ERROR #2.description: Tthe like-named variables in the COBOL group field GROUP-FIELDS-1 are moved to GROUP-FIELDS-2. If there are any variables in GROUP-FIELDS-1 that are larger than the same named variable in GROUP-FIELDS-2 the `ON SIZE ERROR` statement is executed. If `ON SIZE ERROR` isn't coded the program ABENDS. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

ERROR #3.description: The EXCEPTION/ERROR declarative specifies procedures for input/output exception or error handling that are to be executed in addition to the standard z/OS procedures. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

EVERY.description: Part of the COBOL XML statement. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

EXCEPTION #2.description: An EXCEPTION condition occurs when the XML document cannot be generated. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

EXCEPTION #3.description: An EXCEPTION condition occurs when there is a problem closing a QSAM, VSAM or Line Sequential. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

EXIT.description: EXIT statements close the PERFORM CHAIN (internal COBOL iterative control structure). Control is returned to the NSI (Next Sequential Instruction) following the PERFORM statement. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

EXIT PROGRAM.description: EXIT PROGRAM transfers control outside the COBOL program. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

EXIT PROGRAM RETURNING.description: EXIT PROGRAM transfers control outside the COBOL program. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

EXIT METHOD.description: EXIT METHOD transfers control outside the Object COBOL program. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

EXTERNAL.description: The EXTERNAL clause specifies that the main storage associated with a data item is associated with the run unit rather than with any particular program. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

EVALUATE.description: Use the EVALUATE verb in place of a set of IF/ELSE constructs. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

EVALUATE FALSE.description: Use EVALUATE instead of a series of nested IF statements to test multiple conditions and specify distinct actions for each. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

FILE SECTION.description: The FILE SECTION is where you define specifics of each input/output file. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

FILE STATUS.description: `FILE STATUS` defines a two-byte (PIC XX) field that recieves a code from z/OS based on the disposition of the I/O operation. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

MULTIPLE FILE TAPE.description: The `MULTIPLE FILE TAPE` clause specifies that 2 or mote data files share the same physical VOL=SER of tape. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

FILE CONTROL.description: The `FILE-CONTROL` paragraph associates every file in your COBOL program with an external data set. It optionally defines file organization, access mode, etc. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

FILLER.description: A placeholder variable that is not explicitly referred to in a program. FILLER is used to line up variable names with byte-offsets in the physical data record. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

FIRST #2.description: When FIRST is specified and not BEFORE / AFTER - the replacement field changes the left/first occurrence of the inspected field (VAR-1 in this example). https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

FOOTING.description: Part of an FD's "LINAGE" (logical page size) clause - available for QSAM and LINE-SEQUENTIAL files only). `WITH FOOTING` specifies a line # in an output file or printer. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

FOR CHARACTERS AFTER.description: Specifies search characters - in INSPECT verb. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

USE FOR DEBUGGING.description: Specifies debugging to begin on (specified) routine. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

CLOSE x FOR REMOVAL.description: This phrase applies only to TAPE/REEL data sets and is treated as a comment. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

body: PERFORM ${1:B-100PARAGRAPH} VARYING ${2:IDX-1} FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL ${2:IDX-1} > TABLE-MAX-ROWS
FROM #1.description: The "FROM" in a `PERFORM VARYING` clause sets the initial value and the incremental/iterative value(s) for a table subscript or index. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

FROM #2.description: The FROM phrase is equivalent to: `MOVE REC-1 to OUTPUT-REC WRITE OUTPUT-REC.` https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

FROM #3.description: This statement values the receiving-field with one of the system date registers. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

FUNCTION MAX.description: ALPHANUMERIC/INDEX/INTEGER/NATIONAL/NUMERIC MAXIMUM VALUE FROM THE SPECIFIED LIST OF NUMBERS

FUNCTION-POINTER.description: A `FUNCTION-POINTER` is a 4-byte elementary item which can contain the address of a procedure (typically a program) entry point. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

GREATER.description: GREATER is a general comparison operator - treated like the algebraic ">" operator. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

GROUP-USAGE.description: A group item that is described with an explicit or implicit `GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL` clause is a national group item. Note that NATIONAL data items are represented as `UTF-16` characters.  https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

HIGH-VALUE.description: HIGH-VALUE equates to binary (Hex) `FF` - the highest EBCDIC collating sequence value. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

I-O.description: Use the I-O (OPEN) file mode to rewrite QSAM and VSAM file records in place. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-aix/5.1?topic=files-opening-file

I-O-CONTROL.description: The I-O-CONTROL paragraph defines specific data input-output protocols that are applicable for certain files. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

ID DIVISION.description: The ID DIVISION contains paragraphs definining the: PROGRAM-ID, AUTHOR, INSTALLATION, DATE-WRITTEN, and SECURITY paragraphs. Note that ID is an abbreviation of IDENTIFICATION. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

IN #1.description: `COUNT IN` references an integer field that contains the number of characters placed in the current receiving field. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

IN #2.description: `DELIMITER IN` references a PIC X field that contains the DELIMITER character placed found in the UNSTRING field. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

IN #3.description: `TALLYING IN` references a numeric field that contains a total of the number of fields that are acted on during the UNSTRING. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

INDEX.description: `USAGE IS INDEX` creates an index data item, which can used as an index variable into any COBOL internal table (OCCURS clause). https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

OCCURS x INDEXED BY.description: `INDEXED BY` defines an internal COBOL index data item and associates it with a given COBOL table. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED.description: `IS INDEXED` defines a file entry as a VSAM KSDS (Indexed) Data Set in the `ENVIRONMENT DIVISION`'S `SELECT`/`ASSIGN` paragraph. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

READ INTO.description: `READ INTO` reads then copies records from FD buffers into `WORKING-STORAGE` data items. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

RETURN INTO.description: `RETURN INTO` accesses a sorted file record and copies it into a `WORKING-STORAGE` data item. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

INVALID KEY (VSAM).description: `INVALID KEY` can be used in `VSAM KSDS` and `RRDS` files for: `READ`, `START`, `WRITE`, `REWRITE`, and `DELETE` statements. The `INVALID KEY` imperative statement is given control if an I/O error occurs due to a defective `VSAM` file index key. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

INVALID KEY (QSAM).description: For `QSAM` files, the `INVALID KEY` phrase can be used in `WRITE` requests. It is executed if you attempt to write to a I/O disk (VOL=SER) that is full. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

ACCESS IS.description: File specifics with `IS`. Note that `IS` is optional. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

USAGE IS.description: Variable declarations with `IS`. Note that `IS` is optional. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

JNIENVPTR.description: `JNIENVPTR` is a COBOL special register that references the JNI pointer as declared in the `JNI.cpy` copybook. It is used when interfacing Java with COBOL. Note that Special registers are reserved words that name storage areas generated by the compiler. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

body: 01 JSON-CODE PIC S9(9) USAGE BINARY VALUE 0.
JSON-CODE.description: `JSON-CODE` is a special register used to indicate that a `JSON GENERATE` or `JSON PARSE` statement executed successfully or that an exception occurred. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

body: 01 JSON-STATUS PIC S9(9) USAGE BINARY VALUE 0.
JSON-STATUS.description: `JSON-STATUS` is a special register used to indicate that a `JSON GENERATE` or `JSON PARSE` statement executed successfully or that an exception occurred. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

JUST.description: The `JUST`/`JUSTIFIED` clause overrides standard positioning rules for receiving items of category alphabetic, alphanumeric, DBCS, or national. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

ASCENDING KEY #1.description: `ASCENDING KEY` in a table `OCCURS` clause allows you to use a COBOL SEARCH ALL construct. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

ASCENDING KEY #2.description: `ASCENDING KEY` in a table `OCCURS` clause allows you to use a COBOL SEARCH ALL construct. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

RECORD KEY.description: A clause in the `ENVIRONMENT DIVISION`, `FILE-CONTROL` paragraph - `RECORD KEY` declares a field that you define in the `FILE SECTION` to be used to search the indexed/VSAM data thru.  Note that the same technique can be used for SORT Files. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

LABEL RECORDS.description: For QSAM files, `LABEL RECORDS` declares the presence or absence of labels used to identify DASD volumes - for uncataloged files. For VSAM files `LABEL RECORDS` is syntax checked but ignored. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

LEADING.description: `SIGN LEADING`/`TRAILING` declares the position of the operational sign for a numeric variable. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

LEFT.description: LEFT Specifies that an elementary COBOL variable is to be positioned in main storage so that byte one begins at the left word boundary. Note that this is an efficiency coding specification. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

LESS.description: LESS is a general comparison operator - treated like the algebraic "<" operator. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

LINEAGE.description: The LINEAGE clause of a FD entry controls the size/lines of a printed page. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

WRITE LINE.description: Use `LINE` to control the number of blank lines output for a report file. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

LINE SEQUENTIAL.description: `LINE-SEQUENTIAL` defines an input/output file as a line-sequential file - typically Unix or PC. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

CLOSE x WITH LOCK.description: `CLOSE WITH LOCK` ensures that the file cannot be opened again while the program is executing. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

READ LOW-VALUE.description: For Alphanumeric fields - `LOW-VALUE` equates to binary (Hex) `00` - the lowest EBCDIC collating sequence value. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

MOVE LOW-VALUE.description: For Alphanumeric fields - `LOW-VALUE` equates to binary (Hex) `00` - the lowest EBCDIC collating sequence value. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

IF LOW-VALUE.description: For Alphanumeric fields - `LOW-VALUE` equates to binary (Hex) `00` - the lowest EBCDIC collating sequence value. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

body: BY VALUE ARGS AS STRING OCCURS ANY.

RECORDING MODE.description: RECORDING MODE specifies the physical format of records in a QSAM file: F (fixed), V (variable), U (fixed or variable), S (spanned) https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

DEBUGGING MODE.description: `WITH DEBUGGING MODE` activates a compile-switch for debugging lines in the program. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

MORE-LABELS.description: `GO TO MORE-LABELS` statement is specified only in a `COBOL LABEL DECLARATIVE` statement. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

MOVE CORRESPONDING.description: After the above MOVE CORRESPONDING statement, all values in like-named-variables will be copied from GROUP-1 to GROUP-2. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6pg40.pdf

MOVE.description: `MOVE` copies data from one variable to one or more other variables. Note that storage data and Figurative Constants (`SPACES`, `HIGH-VALUES`, `LOW-VALUES`, etc.) can be moved into variables. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

MULTIPLY a BY b GIVING c.description: MULTIPLY a BY b GIVING c

MULTIPLY a BY b GIVING c ON SIZE ERROR.description: If ON SIZE ERROR is specified and a size error condition occurs (typically truncation in the product) the error result is not placed in the product and the imperative statement in the ON SIZE ERROR phrase is executed. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

NATIONAL-EDITED #1.description: `NATIONAL`/`NATIONAL-EDITED` data items are variables whose content is represented in UTF-16 (often referred to as Unicode). https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

NATIONAL-EDITED #2.description: `NATIONAL`/`NATIONAL-EDITED` data (or data items within a group field) are replaced by the same-named variables in VAR-2 in the given example. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

NATIVE.description: `NATIVE` is syntax checked, but has no effect on program execution. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

NEXT SENTENCE.description: `NEXT SENTENCE` transfers control to the next sequential instruction following the closest period (separator). https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

NEXT RECORD.description: `NEXT RECORD` is a phrase that reads the next record from an input file. `NEXT` is optional for QSAM files, but you must specify `NEXT RECORD` to retrieve records sequentially from a VSAM file. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

body: DISPLAY "${1:ERROR IN OPENING FILE}" WITH NO ADVANCING.
NO ADVANCING.description: When used, the positioning of the output device will not be changed. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

NO REWIND.description: `NO REWIND` applies only to `LINE-SEQUENTIAL` and `QSAM` tape files.  Specifically, with `NO REWIND`, `OPEN` filename must be positioned at its beginning record. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

IF var NOT x.description: NOT is a true/false test - testing true if the comparison fails. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

body: NOT ON EXCEPTION ${1:MOVE ZEROS TO VAR-4}
NOT ON EXCEPTION.description: NOT is a true/false test - testing true if the comparison fails. In the snippet, if there is no numeric exception in the subtract, zeros are moved to VAR-4. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

NULL.description: `NULL` which has the value of zero, is a data type used with datatypes of: `POINTER`, `PROCEDURE-POINTER`, `FUNCTION-POINTER`, `OBJECT REFERENCE`, or the `ADDRESS OF` a special register. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

NUMERIC.description: `IF NUMERIC` is a conditional class test which can be applied to variable types: `DISPLAY`, `NATIONAL`, `COMPUTATIONAL-3`, or `PACKED-DECIMAL`. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

body: INITIALIZE ${1:VAR1} REPLACING NUMERIC-EDITED DATA BY ${2:literal or variable}
NUMERIC-EDITED.description: `NUMERIC-EDITED` => Numeric data items with insertion characters. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4?topic=statements-initialize-statement

OBJECT.description: `OBJECT` (after `IDENTIFICATION DIVISION`) introduces an object definition, part of a class definition that defined instance objects. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

OBJECT-COMPUTER.description: The `OBJECT-COMPUTER` paragraph details the mainframe for which the compiled object program is run on. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

OBJECT-REFERENCE.description: An `OBJECT-REFERENCE` data item is a 4 or 8 byte (depending on your z/OS system) that references valid objects. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

OCCURS.description: `OCCURS` is used to code a table by defining a number (N) of repeated subordinate rows. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

OCCURS DEPENDING ON.description: `OCCURS DEPENDING ON` is used to code a table where you do not know how many rows are in the table. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

MOVE x OF y TO.description: OF (qualification) allows you to uniquely specify a variable by referencing higher-level variable-names in a struction. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

SET ADDRESS OF.description: `ADDRESS OF` is a COBOL special register that can be used to reference the address of a data item in the `LINKAGE SECTION`, `LOCAL-STORAGE SECTION`, or `WORKING-STORAGE SECTION`. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

INLINE OFF.description: This COBOL directive OFF prevents the compiler from inlining procedures referenced by PERFORM statements. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

ALL31 OFF.description: Another COBOL directive - specific to external files and DFSMS buffer allocations. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

RECORDS ARE OMITTED.description: Used for Tape files without z/OS data set LABELS. Note that the same OMITTED phrase can be used in SORT/MERGE processing. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

DEPENDING ON.description: `ON` is used as part of a dynamic table declaration. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pd

SET ptr ON.description: ON is used to set a pointer or 88-conditional to True. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pd

ON SIZE ERROR.description: `ON` is used to code: `ON SIZE ERROR`, `ON OVERFLOW` and `ON EXCEPTION` error and exception trapping phrases. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pd

body: OPEN INPUT ${1:fileName}${2|., REVERSED., WITH NO REWIND.|}
OPEN INPUT.description: `OPEN INPUT` initiates the process of reading files. Note that `REVERSED` and `WITH NO REWIND` are optional clauses. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

OPEN OUTPUT.description: `OPEN OUTPUT` initiates the process of writing files. Note that `NO REWIND` is optional. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

OPTIONAL.description: If `SELECT OPTIONAL` is specified in the file-control entry for this file, and the file is not available at runtime, execution of the first READ statement causes an at-end condition - and not an ABEND. Note that this is the case for QSAM and VSAM opened for INPUT, I-O, or EXTEND. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

If x OR y.description: A logical comparison operator. The truth value of OR is true when either or both conditions are met. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

WHEN x OR y.description: A logical comparison operator that is part of an EVALUATE statement. The truth value of OR is true when either or both conditions are met. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

DUPLICATES IN ORDER.description: If duplicate records are found, by coding `DUPLICATES IN ORDER` z/OS will maintain the physical order. Without this phrase, the sorting of duplicate records is undefined. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

ORGANIZATION (QSAM).description: QSAM file accessed sequentially (one record after the next). https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SS6SG3_6.4.0/pdf/pgmvs.pdf

body: ACCESS MODE IS ${4|SEQUENTIAL,RANDOM,DYNAMIC|} RECORD KEY IS ${5:key1}
ORGANIZATION (VSAM).description: VSAM file `ORGANIZATION` clause for a VSAM file accessed thru the file's index (key1).  https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SS6SG3_6.4.0/pdf/pgmvs.pdf

OTHER.description: In an `EVALUATE` statement if no `WHEN` phrase is selected and `WHEN OTHER` is specified, execution continues with the `OTHER` statement. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SS6SG3_6.4.0/pdf/pgmvs.pdf

OUTPUT PROCEDURE.description: In a `SORT` or `MERGE` statement `OUTPUT PROCEDURE` specifies the name of a COBOL SECTION or paragraph that selects and/or modies output records from the `SORT`/`MERGE` operation. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

ON OVERFLOW GO TO (Unstring Statement).description: `ON OVERFLOW` with `UNSTRING` allows you to trap text-parsing errors during runtime.  Note that after `ON OVERFLOW` you can code any imperative statement. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

body: STRING ${2:PATIENT-NO SPACE PATIENT-NAME INV-NO SPACE DATE-PROCESS SPACE}
ON OVERFLOW GO TO (String Statement).description: `ON OVERFLOW` with `STRING` allows you to trap text-parsing errors during runtime.  Note that after `ON OVERFLOW` you can code any imperative statement. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

ON OVERFLOW GO TO (Call Statement).description: `ON OVERFLOW` with `CALL` statements allows you to trap runtime called program name errors. Without `ON OVERFLOW` the program will `ABEND`.  Note that after `ON OVERFLOW` you can code any imperative statement. https://publibfp.dhe.ibm.com/epubs/pdf/igy6lr40.pdf

PERFORM TIMES.description: PERFORM TIMES PROCEDURE NAME X TIMES

body: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING BY VALUE VAL AS ${3:BINARY-LONG}.

SEARCH ALL WHEN.description: SEARCH ALL item1 WHEN item2 EQUAL item3 item4

SUBTRACT.description: SUBTRACT A FROM B GIVING C
